name: Axiom Defense ArcShell Construction Exo-Suit
description:
A Tier 3–4 powered construction exoskeleton with integrated clothing system. The rigid exoframe is brushed gunmetal titanium-alloy over articulated polycarb joint housings, worn over a compression base suit in dark slate gray with hi-vis amber paneling at shoulders and thighs. Hydraulic assist units run along the spine and outer legs, with visible pressure lines in translucent orange.

The base suit is abrasion-resistant stretch-aramid with reinforced knees, elbows, and palms. Neural interface collar connects to BCI for load-sensing feedback. Corponation builds use this for high-rise skeleton work; black-market versions show up on Shelf demolition crews.
functionality: Hydraulic spine and leg assist multiplies carry load up to 400kg. BCI neural collar transmits load-stress feedback directly to the operator. Base suit provides abrasion and impact resistance independent of the frame. Exoframe joints lock for sustained load-hold. Aug-compatible frame channels accommodate prosthetic limb integration.
what_it_says: Either a licensed construction specialist billing Φ900 a day, or someone who acquired this through channels that don't ask questions.
story_hooks: A surplus ArcShell sold to a Shelf demolition crew still has its previous operator's BCI calibration loaded — and that person is listed as missing.
The hydraulic pressure lines on a black-market unit have been modified to handle something other than construction loads.
An Axiom site foreman's exo-suit has been logging GPS coordinates it was never authorized to transmit.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions Combat Exoskeleton Lite CEL-3

physical_description.visual_profile: A muscular, industrial silhouette—rigid exoframe overlaying a fitted compression base. The gunmetal titanium exoskeleton dominates the visual; orange hydraulic lines trace the spine and legs like glowing veins. Hi-vis amber panels at shoulders and thighs create warning-stripe contrast against slate gray. Reads as purposeful, augmented, working-class utility.
physical_description.fit: Form-fitting compression base under rigid exoframe; articulated joints at elbows, knees, hips, and shoulders allow mobility. The exoskeleton sits slightly proud of the body, creating a layered, armored aesthetic. Compression suit hugs the torso and limbs; exoframe adds 2–3 inches of bulk.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed gunmetal titanium-alloy exoframe, polycarb joint housings, stretch-aramid compression base suit, translucent silicone pressure hose (orange), synthetic rubber reinforcement panels
physical_description.texture: Smooth brushed metal on the exoframe with visible machining marks; matte polycarb joints; ribbed stretch-aramid on the base suit; translucent orange hose with visible fluid inside; rubber grip zones on palms and knees
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray (exoframe), dark slate gray (base suit), hi-vis amber (shoulder and thigh panels), translucent orange (hydraulic lines), matte black (joint caps and connectors)
physical_description.closures: Integrated neural interface collar (BCI contact points); friction-fit articulated frame; reinforced elastic cuffs at wrists and ankles; pressure-sealed joints; no visible zippers or manual closures
distinctive_features: Visible hydraulic pressure lines running spine and outer legs
Brushed titanium-alloy exoframe with articulated polycarb joint housings
High-visibility amber paneling at shoulders and thighs (safety compliance or street intimidation)
Neural interface collar for BCI load-sensing feedback
Reinforced palms, knees, elbows in abrasion-resistant rubber
Translucent orange pressure hoses with visible hydraulic fluid
Axiom Defense branding (subtle, on chest and shoulder)
Tool-attachment points and cable routing channels on thighs
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 functional: expensive enough to signal corporate affiliation or salvage-market investment, practical enough for blue-collar legitimacy. Black-market demolition crews modify and re-sell these.
physical_description.cultural_context: Construction worker, demolition operator, or sub-grade salvage worker. Wearing this signals technical skill, augmentation acceptance, and either corpo contract work or black-market familiarity. The exoframe reads as body-honest—this person does heavy lifting for a living.
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory-fresh examples show pristine brushed finish and clear orange hose; field-worn versions display scratched titanium, stained hydraulic fluid in hoses, and patched aramid on knees and elbows. Shelf demolition variants often show crude repairs, rust blooming, and reinforced welds.
